comparator.name: Bachelor Civil Engineering
comparator.sourceNotes: The current University of Twente curriculum page explicitly identifies its course-code and study-unit table as 2026-2027, defines four coherent 15-EC modules in each of years one and two, and gives year three as a 30-EC minor followed by 15 EC of thesis preparation and a 15-EC BSc thesis. The first year covers the construction, water, and traffic domains; the second year integrates delta safety, sustainable civil engineering, area development, and simulation and stochastic modelling. The genuine 30-EC minor space is preserved without inventing a choice. Every listed study unit and the minor account for exactly 180 EC.

exception.reason: Twente's Civil Engineering bachelor integrates calculus and programming with three successive structural-mechanics courses, two fluid-mechanics courses, soil mechanics, fluid measurements, construction design, water systems, transport engineering, spatial development, civil-engineering simulation and large domain projects before a 30-EC civil-engineering graduation phase. UCR offers strong environmental-sustainability, water, earth-science and spatial-planning courses and several useful mathematical and computational tools, but it does not offer the structural, materials, geotechnical, hydraulic, transport or construction-engineering sequence on which the degree's projects depend. A 24-course response would be an environmental studies or sustainable-delta programme with some quantitative tools, not Civil Engineering.
exception.curriculumContext: The official 2026-27 curriculum accounts for all 180 EC: four compulsory 15-EC modules in year one, four compulsory 15-EC modules in year two, a genuine 30-EC minor, 15 EC of thesis preparation and a 15-EC BSc thesis. The programme deliberately integrates technical and non-technical study across construction and infrastructure, water management, and traffic and transport; it has no named graduation route requiring selection.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR course rows, including descriptions, outline-derived profiles, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned semesters. ENSDELT111 Building with Nature and ENSDELT211 Living with Water directly address ecosystem-based flood protection, freshwater management, subsidence and water governance; ENSENVI212 Soils & Aquifers, ENSENVI211 Earth Observation, ENSENVI112 Natural Hazards, Risks & Adaptations, ENSSUST315 Spatial Planning and ENSSUST313 Research in a Sustainable Delta add geoscience, GIS, hazards, planning and applied research. DISGATE102 Mathematical Methods, DISMATH211 Linear Algebra, DISMATH213 Computational & Numerical Methods, DISMATH312 Linear Systems and DISMATH314 Probability & Statistics supply useful quantitative tools, while ENSGATE101/201 and the sustainability sequence cover environmental and social context. The workbook nevertheless contains no structural mechanics, statics or strength-of-materials course; no fluid-mechanics or hydraulics sequence; no construction materials, geotechnical engineering, traffic engineering or transport-design course; and no civil-engineering design studio or civil-engineering thesis sequence. Those are central gaps across every compulsory year-one domain and the integrated second-year projects, not optional specialisms.
